newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Hijack is first from Taiwan to China since 1986.
newsitem.headline: Hijack is first from Taiwan to China since 1986.

text.p: Monday's hijacking of a Far East Air Transport airliner to China from Taiwan was the 13th in a spate of Taiwan Strait air piracy cases in the 1990s.
But it was the first in a decade to go to Communist China from Nationalist Taiwan.
The following is a chronicle of plane commandeerings involving Taiwan and China since the two rivals split after a civil war in 1949:
1949 -- Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist troops, retreating from communist takeover of the Chinese mainland, flee into exile on Taiwan. Political standoff begins.
1958-1989 -- Total of 15 mainland air force and navy pilots defect to Taiwan in 12 military planes. Taipei fetes defectors as freedom fighters and rewards them with huge sums of gold.
1983 -- Six mainland Chinese hijack airliner from Shenyang in northeastern China to Seoul. Taiwan grants hijackers asylum a year later after their release by South Korea's government.
1986 -- Taiwan pilot Wang Xijue defects to China by flying Boeing 747 cargo plane operated by Taiwan's China Airlines to south China.
Wang, Taiwan's first known defector to China, receives hero's welcome and later becomes official in Chinese provincial aeronautic agency.
1991 -- Taiwan announces its intention to stop encouraging Chinese communist military personnel to defect and halt practice of giving financial rewards.
April 6, 1993 - June 6, 1994 -- Chinese hijackers commandeer 12 mainland civilian aircraft to Taiwan, exploiting notoriously lax security at Chinese airports.

Taipei accuses Beijing of deliberately allowing hijackings, possibly to test island's air defences. Beijing condemns Taipei for indirectly encouraging the hijackings by refusing to send hijackers back immediately to China.
December 1994 -- Chinese man armed with petrol bomb tries to hijack mainland airliner to Taiwan but is overpowered by on-board security officers.
January 1995 -- Taiwan, China reach semi-official accord on repatriating hijackers. But agreements have yet to be signed as Beijing broke off semi-official talks in mid-1995.
Taiwan currently holds 16 mainland hijackers in prison on long sentences for air piracy.
March 1996 -- Police at southern China's Zhuhai airport capture two couples brandishing dynamite and daggers, thwarting their attempt to hijack a domestic flight to Taiwan.
November 1996 -- Crew and passengers on Chinese domestic flight subdue man trying to hijack plane to Taiwan.

March 10, 1997 -- Taiwan domestic airliner commandeered to Xiamen in southeast China by jobless journalist claiming to be "victim of political repression" on Taiwan. Suspect asks for political asylum in Xiamen but is arrested by mainland authorities.
